claim: The Omicron BA.1 variant of SARS-CoV-2 escapes convalescent sera and monoclonal antibodies that are effective against earlier strains of the virus.
source: The Omicron BA.1 variant of SARS-CoV-2 escapes convalescent sera and monoclonal antibodies that are effective against earlier strains of the virus.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other studies (Cao et al., 2022; Ao et al., 2022; Planas et al., 2022; Viana et al., 2022) as indicated in the Introduction section.

claim: The immune evasion of Omicron BA.1 is largely a consequence of mutations in the BA.1 receptor binding domain (RBD).
source: This immune evasion is largely a consequence of mutations in the BA.1 receptor binding domain (RBD), the major antigenic target of SARS-CoV-2.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Greaney et al., 2021b; Greaney et al., 2021c; Iketani et al., 2022; Dai and Gao, 2021).

claim: The RBD is the major antigenic target of SARS-CoV-2.
source: This immune evasion is largely a consequence of mutations in the BA.1 receptor binding domain (RBD), the major antigenic target of SARS-CoV-2.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research (Greaney et al., 2021b; Greaney et al., 2021c; Iketani et al., 2022; Dai and Gao, 2021).

claim: The study measured the binding affinity of all possible combinations of 15 RBD mutations (32,768 genotypes) to 4 monoclonal antibodies.
source: Here, we systematically map these interactions by measuring the binding affinity of all possible combinations of these 15 RBD mutations (215=32,768 genotypes) to 4 monoclonal antibodies (LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, REGN10987, and S309) with distinct epitopes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental design and measurements performed in the study.

claim: BA.1 can lose affinity to diverse antibodies by acquiring a few large-effect mutations.
source: We find that BA.1 can lose affinity to diverse antibodies by acquiring a few large-effect mutations and can reduce affinity to others through several small-effect mutations.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: BA.1 can reduce affinity to some antibodies through several small-effect mutations.
source: We find that BA.1 can lose affinity to diverse antibodies by acquiring a few large-effect mutations and can reduce affinity to others through several small-effect mutations.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: There are alternative pathways to antibody escape that do not include every large-effect mutation.
source: However, our results also reveal alternative pathways to antibody escape that does not include every large-effect mutation.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the binding affinity data across all genotypes.

claim: Epistatic interactions constrain affinity decline in S309.
source: Moreover, epistatic interactions are shown to constrain affinity decline in S309 but only modestly shape the affinity landscapes of other antibodies.
evidence: This is based on epistatic modeling and analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Epistatic interactions only modestly shape the affinity landscapes of antibodies other than S309.
source: Moreover, epistatic interactions are shown to constrain affinity decline in S309 but only modestly shape the affinity landscapes of other antibodies.
evidence: This is based on epistatic modeling and analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: The escape of each antibody is mediated by distinct groups of mutations.
source: Together with previous work on the ACE2 affinity landscape, our results suggest that the escape of each antibody is mediated by distinct groups of mutations, whose deleterious effects on ACE2 affinity are compensated by another distinct group of mutations (most notably Q498R and N501Y).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the binding affinity data and comparison with previous ACE2 affinity work.

claim: The deleterious effects of antibody escape mutations on ACE2 affinity are compensated by mutations Q498R and N501Y.
source: Together with previous work on the ACE2 affinity landscape, our results suggest that the escape of each antibody is mediated by distinct groups of mutations, whose deleterious effects on ACE2 affinity are compensated by another distinct group of mutations (most notably Q498R and N501Y).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the binding affinity data and comparison with previous ACE2 affinity work.

claim: The Omicron BA.1 variant emerged in November 2021.
source: In November 2021, the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.1 variant emerged and quickly rose to high frequency worldwide, in part due to its ability to escape preexisting immunity (Cao et al., 2022; Ao et al., 2022; Planas et al., 2022; Viana et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the timing of the variant's emergence, supported by citations.

claim: Omicron BA.1 quickly rose to high frequency worldwide.
source: In November 2021, the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.1 variant emerged and quickly rose to high frequency worldwide, in part due to its ability to escape preexisting immunity (Cao et al., 2022; Ao et al., 2022; Planas et al., 2022; Viana et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies documenting the variant's spread.

claim: Omicron BA.1's rise to high frequency was in part due to its ability to escape preexisting immunity.
source: In November 2021, the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.1 variant emerged and quickly rose to high frequency worldwide, in part due to its ability to escape preexisting immunity (Cao et al., 2022; Ao et al., 2022; Planas et al., 2022; Viana et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on immune escape.

claim: Antibodies targeting the RBD can bind different epitopes and have been grouped into several classes.
source: Antibodies targeting the RBD can bind different epitopes, and they have been grouped into several classes (Barnes et al., 2020b; Barnes et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to classification studies.

claim: Previous SARS-CoV-2 variants with a subset of BA.1 RBD mutations can evade some antibodies of certain epitope classes but still bind to others.
source: Some previous SARS-CoV-2 variants which have a subset of the 15 mutations found in the BA.1 RBD (e.g. K417N, N501Y in Beta and T478K, N501Y in Delta) can evade some antibodies of certain epitope classes but still bind to others (Liu et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2021; Greaney et al., 2022; Greaney et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on Beta and Delta variants.

claim: BA.1 can escape most antibodies that bind to very distinct epitopes.
source: In contrast, BA.1 can escape most antibodies that bind to very distinct epitopes, including antibodies elicited by previously circulating variants (Cao et al., 2022; Dejnirattisai et al., 2022; Cameroni et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on BA.1 immune escape.

claim: Existing studies of SARS-CoV-2 immune escape have focused on measuring the effects of single mutations or small subsets of mutations on antibody escape.
source: Existing studies of SARS-CoV-2 immune escape have focused on measuring the effects of single mutations (or, in some cases, of a small subset of mutations) on antibody escape in the context of specific SARS-CoV-2 variants (Dejnirattisai et al., 2022; Starr et al., 2021b; Starr et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Simultaneous escape of most antibodies is likely to require multiple mutations.
source: However, simultaneous escape of most antibodies is likely to require multiple mutations, and it is unclear how these mutations might interact.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the complexity of immune escape.

claim: The specific combination of mutations in the BA.1 variant can evade various antibodies of distinct epitopes.
source: A large body of work has demonstrated that the specific combination of mutations in the BA.1 variant can evade various antibodies of distinct epitopes (Cao et al., 2022; Planas et al., 2022; Dejnirattisai et al., 2022; Chakraborty et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Several antibody-escape mutations also reduce affinity to ACE2.
source: As we observed in previous work, several of these antibody-escape mutations also reduce affinity to ACE2, suggesting that they were positively selected because they contribute to immune escape (Starr et al., 2020; Mannar et al., 2022; McCallum et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work including the authors' own studies.

claim: Epistatic interactions between mutations dramatically impact ACE2 affinity.
source: Importantly, epistatic interactions between these mutations dramatically impact ACE2 affinity and may also differentially impact the escape of antibodies with very different epitopes (Moulana et al., 2022; Starr et al., 2022a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies including the authors' own work.

claim: Escape from S309 has been difficult to attribute to specific mutations.
source: For example, escape from some antibodies like S309 has been difficult to attribute to specific mutations (McCallum et al., 2022; Case et al., 2022), perhaps because measurements have so far been limited to single mutations.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The study measured equilibrium binding affinities (KD,app) of the spike protein RBD to four therapeutic monoclonal antibodies for all possible evolutionary intermediates between Wuhan Hu-1 RBD and BA.1 variant.
source: Here, to understand how immune pressure may have shaped the evolution of BA.1, we measured the equilibrium binding affinities (KD, app) of the spike protein RBD to four therapeutic monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) with distinct RBD epitopes: LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, REGN10987, and S309, for all possible evolutionary intermediates between the ancestral Wuhan Hu-1 RBD and the BA.1 variant.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach.

claim: LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, and REGN10987 are fully escaped by Omicron BA.1.
source: The first three antibodies are fully escaped by Omicron BA.1, while S309 has reduced affinity.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: S309 has reduced affinity to Omicron BA.1.
source: The first three antibodies are fully escaped by Omicron BA.1, while S309 has reduced affinity.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: For each antibody, only a few mutations significantly impact affinity.
source: We find that for each antibody, only a few mutations significantly impact affinity, and these mutations are largely (but not entirely) orthogonal between the four antibodies.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: The mutations that significantly impact affinity are largely orthogonal between the four antibodies.
source: We find that for each antibody, only a few mutations significantly impact affinity, and these mutations are largely (but not entirely) orthogonal between the four antibodies.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Epistasis plays a limited role in determining affinity to antibodies that are fully escaped by BA.1.
source: Additionally, we find that epistasis plays a limited role in determining affinity to antibodies that are fully escaped by BA.1 but contributes substantially to the reduced affinity for the partially escaped antibody, S309.
evidence: This is a finding from epistatic modeling of the binding affinity data.

claim: Epistasis contributes substantially to the reduced affinity for S309.
source: Additionally, we find that epistasis plays a limited role in determining affinity to antibodies that are fully escaped by BA.1 but contributes substantially to the reduced affinity for the partially escaped antibody, S309.
evidence: This is a finding from epistatic modeling of the binding affinity data.

claim: The BA.1 RBD differs from Wuhan-1 by 15 amino acid substitutions.
source: The BA.1 RBD differs from Wuhan-1 by 15 amino acid substitutions, so this library contains 2 (Dejnirattisai et al., 2022) variants containing all possible combinations of these 15 mutations.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the sequence differences.

claim: The RBD library is displayed on the surface of yeast, with each yeast cell expressing a single variant.
source: This RBD library is displayed on the surface of yeast, such that each yeast cell expresses a single variant.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system.

claim: The study used Tite-seq to measure equilibrium binding affinities.
source: Here, we use Tite-seq (a high-throughput method that integrates flow cytometry and sequencing Moulana et al., 2022; Adams et al., 2016; Phillips et al., 2021; Starr et al., 2022b; see Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) to measure the equilibrium binding affinities of all 32,768 variants to four antibodies with different epitopes (LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, REGN10987, and S309).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method, supported by citations.

claim: The resulting KD,app correlates between biological duplicates.
source: The resulting KD, app correlates between biological duplicates and with isogenic measurements made by flow cytometry (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a validation of the experimental measurements, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The resulting KD,app correlates with isogenic measurements made by flow cytometry.
source: The resulting KD, app correlates between biological duplicates and with isogenic measurements made by flow cytometry (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a validation of the experimental measurements, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The study obtained KD,app for at least ~30,000 variants to each of the mAbs.
source: Of the 32,768 variants in our library, we obtain KD, app for at least ~30,000 variants to each of the mAbs (32,603 for LY-CoV016, 31479 for REGN10987, 27485 for LY-CoV555, and 32650 for S309) after removing variants with poor titration curves (r2<0.8 or σ>1; see Methods).
evidence: This is a report of the data quality and coverage.

claim: 51% of the variants fully escape LY-CoV016.
source: These KD,app range from 0.1 nM to 1 μM (which is our limit of detection and likely corresponds to non-specific binding), with 51% of the variants fully escaping LY-CoV016 (defined as having KD,app above the limit of detection), 65% fully escaping LY-CoV555, 36% fully escaping REGN10897, and no variants fully escaping S309 (Figure 1A; see https://desai-lab.github.io/wuhan_to_omicron/ (Johnson and Dupic, 2022) for an interactive data browser).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: 65% of the variants fully escape LY-CoV555.
source: These KD,app range from 0.1 nM to 1 μM (which is our limit of detection and likely corresponds to non-specific binding), with 51% of the variants fully escaping LY-CoV016 (defined as having KD,app above the limit of detection), 65% fully escaping LY-CoV555, 36% fully escaping REGN10897, and no variants fully escaping S309 (Figure 1A; see https://desai-lab.github.io/wuhan_to_omicron/ (Johnson and Dupic, 2022) for an interactive data browser).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: 36% of the variants fully escape REGN10897.
source: These KD,app range from 0.1 nM to 1 μM (which is our limit of detection and likely corresponds to non-specific binding), with 51% of the variants fully escaping LY-CoV016 (defined as having KD,app above the limit of detection), 65% fully escaping LY-CoV555, 36% fully escaping REGN10897, and no variants fully escaping S309 (Figure 1A; see https://desai-lab.github.io/wuhan_to_omicron/ (Johnson and Dupic, 2022) for an interactive data browser).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: No variants fully escape S309.
source: These KD,app range from 0.1 nM to 1 μM (which is our limit of detection and likely corresponds to non-specific binding), with 51% of the variants fully escaping LY-CoV016 (defined as having KD,app above the limit of detection), 65% fully escaping LY-CoV555, 36% fully escaping REGN10897, and no variants fully escaping S309 (Figure 1A; see https://desai-lab.github.io/wuhan_to_omicron/ (Johnson and Dupic, 2022) for an interactive data browser).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Escape from LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, and REGN10897 is mediated by one or a few strong-effect mutations.
source: Escape from LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, and REGN10897 is mediated by one or a few strong-effect mutations, with other mutations more subtly impacting affinity (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Strong-effect mutations make substantial contact with the corresponding antibody.
source: In general, strong-effect mutations make substantial contact with the corresponding antibody.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and binding data.

claim: Strong-effect mutations are largely distinct for each antibody.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Greaney et al., 2021a; Cameroni et al., 2022; Starr et al., 2021b; Windsor et al., 2022), these strong-effect mutations are largely distinct for each antibody, which presumably reflects their non-overlapping footprints on the RBD (Figure 1C) and suggests that evolution of escape from each antibody can be, to some extent, orthogonal.
evidence: This is a finding from the binding affinity data, supported by citations and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The distinct strong-effect mutations for each antibody reflect their non-overlapping footprints on the RBD.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Greaney et al., 2021a; Cameroni et al., 2022; Starr et al., 2021b; Windsor et al., 2022), these strong-effect mutations are largely distinct for each antibody, which presumably reflects their non-overlapping footprints on the RBD (Figure 1C) and suggests that evolution of escape from each antibody can be, to some extent, orthogonal.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: For S309, ~17% of variants have lower affinity than BA.1.
source: The picture is more complex for S309, where BA.1 has reduced affinity relative to Wuhan Hu-1, but ~17% of variants have lower affinity than BA.1.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: For S309, differences in affinity are not attributable to one or two strong effect mutations.
source: These differences are not attributable to one or two strong effect mutations (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figures 1A-B.

claim: Most mutations reduce affinity to S309.
source: In addition, although most mutations reduce affinity, three mutations have small positive effects (on average across all backgrounds at the other loci): S375F for LY-CoV016 and E484A and N501Y for REGN10987 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: S375F has a small positive effect on LY-CoV016 affinity on average across all backgrounds.
source: In addition, although most mutations reduce affinity, three mutations have small positive effects (on average across all backgrounds at the other loci): S375F for LY-CoV016 and E484A and N501Y for REGN10987 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: E484A has a small positive effect on REGN10987 affinity on average across all backgrounds.
source: In addition, although most mutations reduce affinity, three mutations have small positive effects (on average across all backgrounds at the other loci): S375F for LY-CoV016 and E484A and N501Y for REGN10987 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: N501Y has a small positive effect on REGN10987 affinity on average across all backgrounds.
source: In addition, although most mutations reduce affinity, three mutations have small positive effects (on average across all backgrounds at the other loci): S375F for LY-CoV016 and E484A and N501Y for REGN10987 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Each of the mutations with positive effects on one antibody reduces affinity to at least one of the other antibodies.
source: Intriguingly, each of these mutations reduces affinity to at least one of the other antibodies, and N501Y significantly improves binding to ACE2, suggesting a potential role for trade-offs (and/or epistasis that mitigates these effects on specific backgrounds).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data across multiple antibodies.

claim: N501Y significantly improves binding to ACE2.
source: Intriguingly, each of these mutations reduces affinity to at least one of the other antibodies, and N501Y significantly improves binding to ACE2, suggesting a potential role for trade-offs (and/or epistasis that mitigates these effects on specific backgrounds).
evidence: This is a finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: For each antibody, binding affinities generally decrease as the number of mutations increase.
source: For each antibody, binding affinities generally decrease as the number of mutations increase (Figure 1D–G).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figures 1D-G.

claim: For LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, and REGN10897, the trend of decreasing affinity with increasing mutations is observed amongst variants with and without the large-effect escape mutations.
source: For LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, and REGN10897, this trend is observed amongst variants with and without the large-effect escape mutations (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figures 1D-F.

claim: K417N is sufficient for escape from LY-CoV016.
source: For LY-CoV016, K417N is sufficient for escape (Figure 1D, green), whereas both LY-CoV555 and REGN10987 require at least two mutations for complete escape.
evidence: This is a finding from the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1D.

claim: LY-CoV555 and REGN10987 require at least two mutations for complete escape.
source: For LY-CoV016, K417N is sufficient for escape (Figure 1D, green), whereas both LY-CoV555 and REGN10987 require at least two mutations for complete escape.
evidence: This is a finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: E484A decreases LY-CoV555 affinity by 1000-fold.
source: For LY-CoV555, both E484A and Q493R decrease affinity drastically (1000- and 100-fold, respectively), but only the combination of both mutations lead to complete escape.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: Q493R decreases LY-CoV555 affinity by 100-fold.
source: For LY-CoV555, both E484A and Q493R decrease affinity drastically (1000- and 100-fold, respectively), but only the combination of both mutations lead to complete escape.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: Only the combination of E484A and Q493R leads to complete escape from LY-CoV555.
source: For LY-CoV555, both E484A and Q493R decrease affinity drastically (1000- and 100-fold, respectively), but only the combination of both mutations lead to complete escape.
evidence: This is a finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: Complete escape from REGN10987 requires two mutations: N440K and G446S.
source: Complete escape from REGN10987 also requires two mutations (N440K and G446S), but the individual effects of these mutations are more subtle (reducing affinity by 5- and 10-fold, respectively).
evidence: This is a finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: N440K reduces REGN10987 affinity by 5-fold.
source: Complete escape from REGN10987 also requires two mutations (N440K and G446S), but the individual effects of these mutations are more subtle (reducing affinity by 5- and 10-fold, respectively).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: G446S reduces REGN10987 affinity by 10-fold.
source: Complete escape from REGN10987 also requires two mutations (N440K and G446S), but the individual effects of these mutations are more subtle (reducing affinity by 5- and 10-fold, respectively).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: For S309, affinity declines after a few mutations and in some backgrounds increases upon further mutation.
source: For S309, affinity declines after a few mutations and in some backgrounds increases upon further mutation, suggesting that interactions between these mutations are important in determining affinity (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a finding from the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Almost all variants that do not bind LY-CoV016 contain K417N.
source: We find a largely orthogonal set of one or two mutations are enriched among variants that do not bind each antibody: almost all variants that do not bind LY-CoV016 contain K417N, almost all variants that do not bind REGN10987 contain G446S, and many also contain N440K, and E484A and Q493R are highly enriched among variants that do not bind LY-CoV555.
evidence: This is a finding from enrichment analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Almost all variants that do not bind REGN10987 contain G446S.
source: We find a largely orthogonal set of one or two mutations are enriched among variants that do not bind each antibody: almost all variants that do not bind LY-CoV016 contain K417N, almost all variants that do not bind REGN10987 contain G446S, and many also contain N440K, and E484A and Q493R are highly enriched among variants that do not bind LY-CoV555.
evidence: This is a finding from enrichment analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Many variants that do not bind REGN10987 also contain N440K.
source: We find a largely orthogonal set of one or two mutations are enriched among variants that do not bind each antibody: almost all variants that do not bind LY-CoV016 contain K417N, almost all variants that do not bind REGN10987 contain G446S, and many also contain N440K, and E484A and Q493R are highly enriched among variants that do not bind LY-CoV555.
evidence: This is a finding from enrichment analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: E484A and Q493R are highly enriched among variants that do not bind LY-CoV555.
source: We find a largely orthogonal set of one or two mutations are enriched among variants that do not bind each antibody: almost all variants that do not bind LY-CoV016 contain K417N, almost all variants that do not bind REGN10987 contain G446S, and many also contain N440K, and E484A and Q493R are highly enriched among variants that do not bind LY-CoV555.
evidence: This is a finding from enrichment analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: The escape mutations K417N, G446S, N440K, E484A, and Q493R were already identified on the Wuhan background.
source: These escape mutations were already identified on the Wuhan background (Tada et al., 2022; Starr et al., 2021c; Zhou et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: K417N always abrogates binding to LY-CoV016.
source: Specifically, K417N always abrogates binding to LY-CoV016, G446S and N440K often abrogate binding to REGN10987, and E484A and Q493R often abrogate binding to LY-CoV555.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data across all genetic backgrounds.

claim: G446S and N440K often abrogate binding to REGN10987.
source: Specifically, K417N always abrogates binding to LY-CoV016, G446S and N440K often abrogate binding to REGN10987, and E484A and Q493R often abrogate binding to LY-CoV555.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data across all genetic backgrounds.

claim: E484A and Q493R often abrogate binding to LY-CoV555.
source: Specifically, K417N always abrogates binding to LY-CoV016, G446S and N440K often abrogate binding to REGN10987, and E484A and Q493R often abrogate binding to LY-CoV555.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data across all genetic backgrounds.

claim: G446S is slightly enriched among LY-CoV555 binders.
source: For example, G446S is slightly enriched among LY-CoV555 binders, while mutation E484A is slightly depleted among variants that do not bind REGN10987 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from enrichment analysis, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: E484A is slightly depleted among variants that do not bind REGN10987.
source: For example, G446S is slightly enriched among LY-CoV555 binders, while mutation E484A is slightly depleted among variants that do not bind REGN10987 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from enrichment analysis, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: G446S sometimes abrogates binding to LY-CoV555.
source: Consistent with this, G446S sometimes abrogates binding to LY-CoV555 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: S375F is weakly enriched among variants that do not bind REGN10987 and LY-CoV555.
source: In addition, some apparently smaller-effect mutations can be involved in abolishing binding to multiple antibodies. For example, S375F is weakly enriched among variants that do not bind REGN10987 and LY-CoV555 and often abrogates binding to these two antibodies, with G496S, Q498R, and N501Y also playing a role.
evidence: This is a finding from enrichment analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: S375F often abrogates binding to REGN10987 and LY-CoV555.
source: In addition, some apparently smaller-effect mutations can be involved in abolishing binding to multiple antibodies. For example, S375F is weakly enriched among variants that do not bind REGN10987 and LY-CoV555 and often abrogates binding to these two antibodies, with G496S, Q498R, and N501Y also playing a role.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: G496S, Q498R, and N501Y play a role in abolishing binding to REGN10987 and LY-CoV555.
source: In addition, some apparently smaller-effect mutations can be involved in abolishing binding to multiple antibodies. For example, S375F is weakly enriched among variants that do not bind REGN10987 and LY-CoV555 and often abrogates binding to these two antibodies, with G496S, Q498R, and N501Y also playing a role.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Variants can escape REGN10987 by acquiring G446S and N440K (100%).
source: For example, variants can escape REGN10987 by acquiring G446S and N440K (100%), or alternatively, with S375F and G446S (89%, as additional mutations may also be required).
evidence: This is a finding from decision tree analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Variants can escape REGN10987 by acquiring S375F and G446S (89%).
source: For example, variants can escape REGN10987 by acquiring G446S and N440K (100%), or alternatively, with S375F and G446S (89%, as additional mutations may also be required).
evidence: This is a finding from decision tree analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Different sets of mutations can lead to escape from LY-CoV555, including Q493R and G446S or E484A and S375F.
source: For LY-CoV555, different sets of mutations can lead to escape (e.g. Q493R and G446S or E484A and S375F).
evidence: This is a finding from decision tree analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Some escape mutations for LY-CoV555 partially overlap with those for REGN10987.
source: Some of these mutations partially overlap with those for REGN10987 (i.e. they are not fully orthogonal), suggesting that selection pressure from one antibody could promote subsequent escape of another.
evidence: This is an inference from the binding affinity data.

claim: Adding epistatic interactions improves the predictive power of the model for all four antibodies as well as for binding to ACE2.
source: We find that adding epistatic interactions improves the predictive power of the model for all four antibodies as well as for binding to ACE2, though the optimal order varies (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from epistatic modeling, shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The optimal order of epistatic interactions varies among antibodies and ACE2.
source: We find that adding epistatic interactions improves the predictive power of the model for all four antibodies as well as for binding to ACE2, though the optimal order varies (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from epistatic modeling, shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Epistasis plays a significant role in determining affinity for all antibodies and ACE2.
source: This indicates that epistasis does play a significant role in all cases (up to second order for REGN10987, to third order for LY-CoV555, and to fourth or higher order for LY-CoV016, S309, and ACE2).
evidence: This is a conclusion from epistatic modeling analysis.

claim: Higher-order epistasis plays a much stronger role in determining affinity for ACE2 than for the three antibodies fully escaped by BA.1.
source: Notably, we find that the higher-order epistasis plays a much stronger role in determining affinity for ACE2 than for the three antibodies fully escaped by BA.1 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from epistatic modeling, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Antibody escape is more simply determined by the additive effects of individual mutations, while maintaining ACE2 affinity involves more complex epistatic interactions.
source: In other words, while epistasis is relevant for all measured phenotypes, antibody escape is more simply determined by the additive effects of individual mutations, while maintaining ACE2 affinity involves more complex epistatic interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from epistatic modeling analysis.

claim: Four neighboring mutations (G339D, S371L, S373P, and S375F) interact non-additively to produce the reduction in affinity to S309 observed in BA.1 relative to Wuhan Hu-1.
source: In Figure 3C, we highlight four neighboring mutations (G339D, S371L, S373P, and S375F) which interact non-additively to produce the reduction in affinity observed in BA.1 relative to Wuhan Hu-1.
evidence: This is a finding from epistatic analysis, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Each of the mutations G339D, S371L, S373P, and S375F weakly reduces affinity to S309 on their own.
source: Each of these mutations weakly reduces affinity on their own, and specific combinations of these mutations can reduce affinity by up to two orders of magnitude, but the reduction in affinity resulting from all four mutations is less than some sets of three mutations.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Specific combinations of G339D, S371L, S373P, and S375F can reduce S309 affinity by up to two orders of magnitude.
source: Each of these mutations weakly reduces affinity on their own, and specific combinations of these mutations can reduce affinity by up to two orders of magnitude, but the reduction in affinity resulting from all four mutations is less than some sets of three mutations.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: The reduction in S309 affinity resulting from all four mutations (G339D, S371L, S373P, and S375F) is less than some sets of three mutations.
source: Each of these mutations weakly reduces affinity on their own, and specific combinations of these mutations can reduce affinity by up to two orders of magnitude, but the reduction in affinity resulting from all four mutations is less than some sets of three mutations.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: S371L reduces S309 affinity on the Wuhan Hu-1 background but increases affinity on the background containing G339D, S373P, and S375F.
source: For example, S371L reduces affinity on the Wuhan Hu-1 background but increases affinity on the background containing G339D, S373P, and S375F (and without G339D, S371L increases affinity in the presence of S373P if S375F is absent but not if it is present).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data demonstrating epistasis.

claim: Some variants lacking S371L evade S309 more effectively than BA.1.
source: Thus, some variants lacking S371L evade S309 more effectively than BA.1, and interestingly we note that this mutation is absent in BA.2 and BA.3 and replaced instead by S371F.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: S371L is absent in BA.2 and BA.3 and replaced instead by S371F.
source: Thus, some variants lacking S371L evade S309 more effectively than BA.1, and interestingly we note that this mutation is absent in BA.2 and BA.3 and replaced instead by S371F.
evidence: This is a factual observation about other Omicron sublineages.

claim: Antibody escape mutations typically reduce ACE2 affinity.
source: In previous work, we found that antibody escape mutations (as defined in earlier studies) typically reduce ACE2 affinity, suggesting that viral evolution is constrained by a tradeoff between immune evasion and the ability to enter host cells.
evidence: This is supported by reference to previous work.

claim: Variants that escape one or more antibodies but have few additional mutations have reduced ACE2 affinity relative to Wuhan Hu-1.
source: Consistent with this, we find here that variants that escape one or more antibodies (as defined by the data reported in this work) but have few additional mutations have reduced ACE2 affinity relative to Wuhan Hu-1.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: As additional BA.1 mutations are accumulated, the ACE2 binding affinity tends to increase until it exceeds the Wuhan Hu-1 value even in the presence of multiple antibody escape mutations.
source: However, as additional BA.1 mutations are accumulated, the ACE2 binding affinity tends to increase until it exceeds the Wuhan Hu-1 value even in the presence of multiple antibody escape mutations (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The evolution of the BA.1 variant is driven both by immune escape and the need for compensatory mutations that mitigate the negative effects of the escape mutations on ACE2 binding.
source: This suggests that the evolution of the BA.1 variant is driven both by immune escape and the need for compensatory mutations that mitigate the negative effects of the escape mutations on ACE2 binding.
evidence: This is an inference from the binding affinity data.

claim: Escape from LY-CoV016 or LY-CoV555 reduces ACE2 binding affinity in the absence of compensatory mutations (Q498R and N501Y) but not in their presence.
source: For example, escape from LY-CoV016 or LY-CoV555 reduces ACE2 binding affinity in the absence of compensatory mutations (Q498R and N501Y) but not in their presence (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 4B.

claim: REGN10987 escape does not strongly reduce affinity to ACE2, whether or not Q498R and N501Y are present.
source: In contrast, REGN10987 escape does not strongly reduce affinity to ACE2, whether or not Q498R and N501Y are present.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Escaping all three antibodies substantially reduces ACE2 affinity in the absence of Q498R and N501Y.
source: However, this tradeoff is likely relevant overall, as escaping all three antibodies substantially reduces ACE2 affinity in the absence of Q498R and N501Y, while the reduction in ACE2 affinity is minimal in their presence.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: The reduction in ACE2 affinity from escaping all three antibodies is minimal in the presence of Q498R and N501Y.
source: However, this tradeoff is likely relevant overall, as escaping all three antibodies substantially reduces ACE2 affinity in the absence of Q498R and N501Y, while the reduction in ACE2 affinity is minimal in their presence.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: The frequency of most escape mutations (G446S, E484A, and Q493R) is higher across the SARS-CoV-2 phylogeny in the presence of compensatory mutations.
source: Consistent with this general picture, the frequency of most escape mutations (G446S, E484A, and Q493R) is higher across the SARS-CoV-2 phylogeny in the presence of compensatory mutations (Figure 4D), though we note that this is not universally true (e.g. the frequency of N440K is only slightly higher in the presence of compensatory mutations, and the frequency of K417N is lower with the compensatory mutations).
evidence: This is a finding from phylogenetic analysis, shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The frequency of N440K is only slightly higher in the presence of compensatory mutations.
source: Consistent with this general picture, the frequency of most escape mutations (G446S, E484A, and Q493R) is higher across the SARS-CoV-2 phylogeny in the presence of compensatory mutations (Figure 4D), though we note that this is not universally true (e.g. the frequency of N440K is only slightly higher in the presence of compensatory mutations, and the frequency of K417N is lower with the compensatory mutations).
evidence: This is a finding from phylogenetic analysis, shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The frequency of K417N is lower with the compensatory mutations.
source: Consistent with this general picture, the frequency of most escape mutations (G446S, E484A, and Q493R) is higher across the SARS-CoV-2 phylogeny in the presence of compensatory mutations (Figure 4D), though we note that this is not universally true (e.g. the frequency of N440K is only slightly higher in the presence of compensatory mutations, and the frequency of K417N is lower with the compensatory mutations).
evidence: This is a finding from phylogenetic analysis, shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Antibody binding affinity is not strongly correlated with ACE2 affinity.
source: Although antibody escape mutations do tend to reduce ACE2 affinity, antibody binding affinity (but not complete escape) is not strongly correlated with ACE2 affinity (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 4C.

claim: For LY-CoV016 and LY-CoV555, there is a weak overall positive correlation between antibody affinity and ACE2 affinity.
source: For LY-CoV016 and LY–CoV555, there is a weak overall positive correlation (i.e. lower antibody affinity also tends to correspond to reduced ACE2 affinity).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: The correlation between LY-CoV016/LY-CoV555 affinity and ACE2 affinity is dominated by variants that lack compensatory mutations at sites 498 and 501.
source: However, this correlation is dominated by the variants that lack the compensatory mutations at sites 498 and 501; in the presence of Q498R and N501Y, the correlation is reduced, especially for LY-CoV016.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: For REGN10987 and S309, there is a weak overall positive correlation between antibody affinity and ACE2 affinity, which is not dependent on Q498R and N501Y.
source: For REGN10987 and S309, there is a similar weak overall positive correlation, which is not dependent on Q498R and N501Y.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: Compensatory mutations Q498R and N501Y largely drive the variance in ACE2 affinity.
source: We also note that while compensatory mutations Q498R and N501Y largely drive the variance in ACE2 affinity, they minimally impact antibody binding affinities (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Q498R and N501Y minimally impact antibody binding affinities.
source: We also note that while compensatory mutations Q498R and N501Y largely drive the variance in ACE2 affinity, they minimally impact antibody binding affinities (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, shown in Figure 4D.

claim: BA.1 escape from LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, and REGN10987 is driven by a relatively small set of mutations.
source: Overall, we find that BA.1 escape from LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, and REGN10987 is driven by a relatively small set of mutations: K417N for LY-CoV016, N440K and G446S for REGN10987, and E484A and Q493R for LY-CoV555.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the binding affinity data.

claim: The mutations driving escape from LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, and REGN10987 have largely orthogonal effects on affinity to the three antibodies.
source: These mutations have largely orthogonal effects on affinity to the three antibodies, suggesting that the evolution of escape to each can occur independently, as might be expected given the distinct epitopes they target (Barnes et al., 2020b; Cameroni et al., 2022; Starr et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the binding affinity data, supported by citations.

claim: Four mutations (S375F, T478K, E484A, and N501Y) improve affinity to one antibody and reduce affinity to another.
source: However, despite these largely orthogonal effects of large-effect mutations on antibody escape, we do observe limited trade-offs among LY-CoV016, LY-CoV555, and REGN10987, with four mutations (S375F, T478K, E484A, and N501Y) improving affinity to one antibody and reducing affinity to another.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: For all antibodies studied, outside of a few large-effect mutations that abrogate or nearly abrogate binding, most mutations weakly impact binding affinity.
source: In fact, for all antibodies studied here, outside of a few large-effect mutations that abrogate or nearly abrogate binding, most mutations weakly impact binding affinity and, even collectively, are insufficient to abrogate it.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: Trade-offs between binding ACE2 and escaping antibodies are much stronger than the orthogonality of antibody escape.
source: In contrast to the orthogonality of antibody escape, trade-offs between binding ACE2 and escaping antibodies are much stronger.
evidence: This is a conclusion from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: The strong-effect mutations substantially reduce ACE2 affinity.
source: While the mutations with a small effect on antibody escape are mostly uncorrelated to ACE2 affinity, the strong-effect mutations substantially reduce ACE2 affinity.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: ACE2 affinity is lower for variants that escape a larger number of antibodies unless compensatory mutations are acquired.
source: Thus, ACE2 affinity is lower for variants that escape a larger number of antibodies unless compensatory mutations are acquired, suggesting that these compensatory mutations potentiated the establishment of the antibody escape mutations (Moulana et al., 2022; Javanmardi et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data, supported by citations.

claim: The reduced affinity of S309 to Omicron could not be attributed to specific mutations prior to this work.
source: Prior to this work, the reduced affinity of S309 to Omicron could not be attributed to specific mutations (Cameroni et al., 2022; Case et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The reduction in S309 affinity is attributable to a fourth-order epistatic interaction.
source: Here, we find that this ambiguity can be resolved by examining higher-order interactions between mutations, as the reduction in affinity is attributable to a fourth-order epistatic interaction.
evidence: This is a finding from epistatic modeling of the binding affinity data.

claim: The potential for future SARS-CoV-2 lineages to escape S309 and similar antibodies could depend on epistatic interactions between emerging mutations.
source: This finding suggests that the potential for future SARS-CoV-2 lineages to escape S309 and similar antibodies could depend on epistatic interactions between emerging mutations.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the findings.

claim: Binding affinities may not always perfectly reflect viral escape from antibody neutralization.
source: We note that our study focuses only on binding affinities, which may not always perfectly reflect viral escape from antibody neutralization (Steckbeck et al., 2005; Culp et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: Neutralization cannot occur in the absence of affinity.
source: However, because neutralization cannot occur in the absence of affinity, our measurements are likely to be relevant for understanding the reduced sensitivity of BA.1 to these antibodies.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on biological principles.

claim: For the first three antibodies, one or two mutations are sufficient for total escape.
source: In spite of these limitations, our binding affinity landscapes reveal that BA.1 can escape diverse antibodies by acquiring a few large-effect mutations and can reduce affinity to others by accumulating several small-effect mutations. For the first three antibodies, one or two mutations are sufficient for total escape.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: In some cases, additional mutations can restore affinity.
source: However, in some cases, additional mutations can restore affinity, and in others, specific combinations of large- and small-effect mutations can abrogate affinity.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of the binding affinity data.

claim: For S309, four mutations drive the decline in affinity yet are also involved in higher-order epistatic interactions that counteract this decline.
source: In contrast, for the S309 antibody, four mutations drive the decline in affinity yet are also involved in higher-order epistatic interactions that counteract this decline.
evidence: This is a finding from epistatic modeling of the binding affinity data.

claim: Epistasis in S309 results in an affinity threshold, beyond which additional mutations do not reduce affinity.
source: This epistasis results in an affinity threshold, beyond which additional mutations do not reduce affinity.
evidence: This is a finding from epistatic modeling of the binding affinity data.

claim: The RBD ACE2 affinity landscape is defined by several epistatic interactions.
source: While our earlier work demonstrates that the RBD ACE2 affinity landscape is defined by several epistatic interactions (Moulana et al., 2022), our results here show that escape from antibody binding can in many (but not all) cases be driven by individual mutations.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Escape from antibody binding can in many cases be driven by individual mutations.
source: While our earlier work demonstrates that the RBD ACE2 affinity landscape is defined by several epistatic interactions (Moulana et al., 2022), our results here show that escape from antibody binding can in many (but not all) cases be driven by individual mutations.
evidence: This is a finding from the binding affinity data.

claim: The prevalence of epistasis in the ACE2 affinity landscape may be a consequence of the long history of spike protein evolution to bind ACE2.
source: One possibility is that the prevalence of epistasis in the ACE2 affinity landscape is a consequence of the long history of spike protein evolution to bind ACE2, which may have selected for more complex epistatic interactions among the acquired mutations over time (in contrast, evolution to escape antibodies is relatively recent).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed patterns.

claim: The relative simplicity of the antibody escape landscapes could be attributed to the fact that beneficial mutations in this case disrupt rather than maintain or improve an interaction.
source: Alternatively, the relative simplicity of the antibody escape landscapes could be attributed to the fact that beneficial mutations in this case disrupt (rather than maintain or improve) an interaction (Greaney et al., 2021a; Starr et al., 2021b; Starr et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation supported by citations.
